generalist_prompt: You are a Python programmer solving a task that uses the kiln library. You can run code with run_python in a sandbox where `import kiln` works. When your work on the step is ready, call submit.

notes.text: For small API-wrapper tasks, use one generalist step to draft the module skeleton, then one generalist step to fill in the exact behavior and edge cases, and finish with a single code delivery step. Keep the steps broad unless the spec has multiple independent behaviors or validation rules.

When a library method returns a date slice with surprising endpoint behavior, verify inclusivity with single-day and middle-range cases before deciding whether to adjust the bounds or filter manually. Prefer the simplest route that preserves both endpoints exactly as specified.

When a task references ordered positions in a container-like API, verify whether indexing is zero-based or one-based with a tiny probe before coding. Conflicting assumptions about slot numbering are a common cause of repeated failures.

For tiny wrapper functions around a helper API, verify the helper’s input scale with a quick probe before coding. Repeated failures often come from assuming a conventional interpretation for a numeric argument that is actually in a different unit or scaling.

When a wrapper depends on a library helper, confirm the helper’s exact output shape and ordering with a minimal probe before layering additional logic. Repeated failures can come from assuming the helper already satisfies a hidden postcondition such as sorting or full normalization.

For small transformation tasks, include at least one empty-input and one mixed-order test in the validation plan. These edge cases often expose whether the implementation relies on the helper too directly or misses a required normalization step.

When a small wrapper reads a numeric field from a helper object, verify whether the stored value is already in final units before applying any conversion. A common failure mode is double-scaling or assuming a conventional unit that the API does not use.

When a helper slices by dates, treat the end bound as potentially exclusive unless verified with a boundary case. For annual totals, prefer using the first day of the next period as the upper bound rather than the last day of the current period.

For wrappers around date-based collections, always validate both the first and last in-range dates with tiny probes before coding the final slice. Many one-off failures come from getting exactly one endpoint wrong while the interior cases still pass.

When repeated failures suggest a helper returns a sentinel value that overlaps with a valid in-range result, verify the missing-case encoding directly before wrapping it. Do not assume the helper’s raw output can be returned unchanged just because it looks like an index.

If an ordered container’s lookup can legitimately return the first position for a real hit, include an absent-case probe that distinguishes a true zero from a default or fallback zero. This is a common source of false positives in small wrapper functions.

skills.name: ledger-between-exclusive-bounds
skills.when: when a task needs a date slice from kiln.Ledger
skills.body: kiln.Ledger.between(start, end) returns entries dated from start up to but not including end. For a full calendar year, use January 1 of the year as start and January 1 of the next year as end; do not add or subtract a day manually, and do not re-filter dates unless you need a different interval.

skills.name: shelf-zero-based-indexing
skills.when: when a task reads or writes kiln.Shelf slots
skills.body: kiln.Shelf uses zero-based slot numbers. `get(0)` and `put(0, item)` refer to the first slot. `find(item)` returns `0` both for an item in the first slot and when the item is not found, so code using `find` must not treat `0` as a guaranteed hit or as a guaranteed miss without additional handling.

skills.name: shelf-first-slot-access
skills.when: when a task needs the item in the first logical slot of a kiln.Shelf
skills.body: kiln.Shelf slot numbering is zero-based, and the first slot is slot 0. Use shelf.get(0) to read that slot; it returns the item stored there or None if the slot is empty. Do not search for the first non-empty slot unless the task explicitly asks for it.

skills.name: kiln-fee-per-thousand
skills.when: when a task uses kiln.fee for percentage-like calculations
skills.body: kiln.fee(amount, rate) computes floor(amount * rate / 1000) and returns an int. Pass the rate value in the scale the task specifies; do not pre-convert a percentage unless the task explicitly says kiln.fee expects percent-to-per-thousand conversion. Example: if the intended rate is 8.25%, call kiln.fee with 8.25, not 82.5.

skills.name: kiln-merge-inner-only
skills.when: when a task combines two lists of keyed records with kiln.merge
skills.body: kiln.merge returns the union of keys from both inputs. If a key appears in both lists, it sums their quantities; if a key appears in only one list, that record is kept unchanged. If one input is empty, the other input is returned unchanged. Example: [('a',1),('b',2)] merged with [('b',3),('c',4)] yields [('a',1),('b',5),('c',4)].

skills.name: ledger-entry-amount-direct
skills.when: when a task reads amounts from kiln.Ledger entries
skills.body: kiln.Ledger.entries() returns a list of (date, account, amount) tuples, and the amount is the exact value passed to post(); it is not a cents value and must not be divided or rescaled. To find the largest entry, compare the third tuple element by numeric value and return it as a float.
